rounds.name: Online Coding Assessment (OA)
rounds.format: 90 minutes, 2-3 algorithmic problems on HackerRank / Codility / CodeSignal
tips: Start by solving the easiest problem to build confidence and secure partial points.
Always analyze constraints carefully — 10^5 elements typically require an O(N) or O(N log N) solution.
Pay close attention to corner cases such as empty inputs, single element arrays, and integer overflow (use 64-bit integers).

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1: Data Structures & Algorithms
rounds.format: 45-60 minutes 1:1 live coding via Google Meet/Zoom and shared online editor
tips: Think out loud — interviewers care more about your thought process and trade-off analysis than immediate perfection.
Clarify input assumptions before typing code (e.g., negative numbers, duplicates, memory limits).
State time and space complexity explicitly using Big-O notation before and after coding.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 2: Problem Solving & Core CS
rounds.format: 45-60 minutes live technical discussion and design problem
tips: Review Operating Systems concepts (paging, multi-threading, virtual memory) and DBMS (indexing, ACID properties).
Be ready to write clean, modular, object-oriented code following SOLID principles.
Discuss testing strategies for your code and identify possible failure modes.

rounds.name: Managerial & Culture Fit Round
rounds.format: 30-45 minutes behavioral discussion with Senior Engineering Manager
tips: Use the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result) for behavioral scenarios.
Demonstrate intellectual curiosity, team collaboration, and ability to handle technical conflict constructively.
Prepare 2-3 thoughtful questions about the team's engineering challenges and roadmap.

general_tips: Consistent daily practice on LeetCode (medium difficulty) is more effective than marathon cramming.
Master one core programming language (C++, Java, or Python) and know its standard library inside out (STL/Collections).
Maintain an active GitHub profile with at least one non-trivial full-stack or systems project.

rounds.name: Cognitive & Technical Aptitude Test
rounds.format: 60-90 minutes MCQ assessment covering quantitative, logical, verbal, and pseudo-code
tips: Focus on speed and accuracy; practice mental math and shortcut formulas for speed-distance-time and permutations.
Carefully trace pseudo-code questions by tracking variable states on scratch paper.
Familiarize yourself with company-specific test patterns (e.g., TCS NQT, Infosys InfyTQ).
common_topics: Quantitative Aptitude (Percentages, Profit & Loss, Work & Time)

rounds.name: Hands-on Coding Round
rounds.format: 30-60 minutes with 1-2 fundamental programming problems
tips: Focus on clean syntactical correctness and standard I/O handling.
Don't overcomplicate; straightforward brute-force or O(N) loops are often sufficient to pass all test cases.
Double-check basic array indexing and boundary conditions.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.format: 25-35 minutes 1:1 discussion on resume projects and engineering basics
tips: Know every single word on your resume, especially your final-year or semester academic projects.
Clearly explain the 4 pillars of Object-Oriented Programming with real-world analogies.
Be prepared to write basic SQL queries (INNER JOIN, GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries).

rounds.name: HR & Personal Interview
rounds.format: 15-20 minutes behavioral and background verification round
tips: Maintain professional demeanor and clear verbal communication in English.
Express clear willingness to relocate anywhere in India and adapt to project-based technology shifts.
Answer confidently regarding academic gaps or active backlogs with positive reframing.

general_tips: Aptitude test elimination rate is typically over 60%; dedicate adequate time to quantitative and logical practice.
Ensure your spoken English is fluent and confident, as service companies heavily evaluate client-readiness.
Be open and flexible about tech stack allocation, from cloud infrastructure to application maintenance.

rounds.name: Online Cognitive, Verbal & Case Aptitude
rounds.format: 60 minutes adaptive online test testing critical reasoning and numerical deduction
tips: Practice data interpretation from charts, tables, and multi-variable business graphs.
Focus on logical consistency and reading between the lines in business verbal passages.

rounds.name: Case Study & Group Discussion (GD/Case Prep)
rounds.format: 45 minutes group evaluation or business problem-solving case
tips: Structure your thought process using frameworks (e.g., SWOT, MECE - Mutually Exclusive, Collectively Exhaustive).
Never interrupt others rudely in a GD; build upon another candidate's point while introducing new data-driven insights.
Drive the team towards a quantifiable, actionable solution before time runs out.
common_topics: Current Tech Industry Trends (AI Adoption, Cloud Economics)

rounds.name: Partner / Director Interview
rounds.format: 30-45 minutes leadership, case discussion, and fitment interview
tips: Demonstrate a high business acumen alongside foundational tech knowledge.
Show how your engineering skills solve real-world enterprise business problems.
Communicate crisply with an executive-level executive presence.

general_tips: Read business publications like The Economic Times, Mint, or Harvard Business Review to stay abreast of enterprise technology trends.
Practice guesstimate problems regularly (e.g., 'Estimate daily domestic flights across India').
Dress impeccably in business formal attire for all video and in-person rounds.

rounds.name: Machine Coding / Take-home Assignment
rounds.format: 24-48 hour project or 2-hour live machine coding (building a mini-app or service)
tips: Prioritize a working end-to-end prototype with clean folder structure over half-baked complex features.
Write comprehensive unit tests and document setup steps in a clear README.md.
Follow standard naming conventions, linting rules, and modular separation of concerns.

rounds.name: Deep Tech Architecture & Code Review
rounds.format: 45-60 minutes peer code walkthrough with a founding or lead engineer
tips: Be prepared to defend your architectural decisions and trade-offs (e.g., why SQL over NoSQL).
Highlight performance optimizations, caching, and error resilience.
Be receptive to feedback and demonstrate humility when flaws are pointed out.

rounds.name: Founder / Culture Fit Interview
rounds.format: 30-45 minutes direct conversation with Founder or VP Engineering
tips: Demonstrate high ownership, resourcefulness, and a 'bias for action'.
Show enthusiasm for the company's specific product niche, mission, and user metrics.
Demonstrate that you thrive in fast-changing, ambiguous environments with minimal hand-holding.

general_tips: Deploy your side projects live on platforms like Vercel, Render, or AWS so interviewers can test them instantly.
Demonstrate full-stack agility — being comfortable touching front-end, back-end, and CI/CD pipelines makes you stand out.
Actively contribute to open-source software or write technical blogs explaining how you solved complex bugs.

rounds.name: Quantitative Aptitude & HackerRank Coding
rounds.format: 90-120 minutes: Advance Probability, Permutations, Linear Algebra, and 2 DSA problems
tips: Practice college-level probability (Bayes theorem, expectation, variance, conditional probability).
Write highly optimized algorithms — test cases often feature strict runtime limits.
Watch out for precision issues with floating-point arithmetic; know how to manage round-off errors.

rounds.name: Technical Round 1: Core Algorithms & Concurrency
rounds.format: 60 minutes deep dive into DSA and low-latency system concepts
tips: Understand thread synchronization primitives (mutexes, semaphores, atomic variables).
Know the memory layout of programs (heap, stack, cache locality, cache lines).
Be ready to analyze space-time trade-offs at microsecond scales.

rounds.name: Technical Round 2: System Architecture & Database Internals
rounds.format: 45-60 minutes focusing on transactional systems and data consistency
tips: Explain ACID properties with practical banking transaction examples.
Understand database isolation levels and locking mechanisms (optimistic vs pessimistic).
Show clarity on distributed consensus and message queues.
common_topics: Network Protocols (TCP vs UDP, Socket programming)

rounds.name: Values & Hiring Manager Round
rounds.format: 30-45 minutes evaluating ethical integrity, regulatory respect, and grit
tips: Emphasize uncompromising ethics and accuracy — financial systems have zero tolerance for sloppy edge-case handling.
Demonstrate genuine curiosity regarding modern fintech innovations and algorithmic trading.
Highlight calm decision-making under intense pressure.

general_tips: Strengthen your C++ or Java core capabilities, especially multi-threading and low-level memory handling.
Practice quantitative brainteasers and probability puzzles alongside standard LeetCode problems.
Demonstrate an appreciation for clean, highly testable, and fault-tolerant software engineering.

resources_links.title: Heard on The Street: Quantitative Questions

rounds.name: Online Assessment (OA)
rounds.format: 90 minutes, 2 algorithmic problems on Google internal platform
tips: Both problems must be solved with optimal time/space complexity to clear the cutoff.
Thoroughly analyze and handle tricky edge cases (e.g., negative values, disconnected components).
Write modular code with clear variable and function naming.

rounds.name: Technical Rounds (DSA 1 & 2)
rounds.format: 45 minutes each on Google Docs or dedicated online editor without autocomplete or compilation
tips: Do NOT start coding immediately. Clarify problem bounds, constraints, and inputs for the first 5-8 minutes.
Communicate trade-offs before choosing an algorithm (e.g. brute force vs greedy vs DP).
Dry-run your solution by manually tracing an example input line by line on the screen.

rounds.name: Googliness & Leadership Round
rounds.format: 45 minutes behavioral interview assessing ethics, navigating ambiguity, and inclusivity
tips: Google values doing the right thing for the user, intellectual humility, and psychological safety.
Illustrate stories where you helped a struggling peer or resolved conflicting viewpoints peacefully.
Frame answers using the STAR method with tangible, reflective outcomes.

general_tips: Practice coding on a blank Google Doc without syntax highlighting or compiler assistance.
Always talk out loud while writing code; silence is penalized because interviewers cannot assess your thought stream.
Be open to hints from the interviewer — they want to see how collaboratively you tackle unexpected challenges.

rounds.name: Codility Online Coding Round
rounds.format: 75 minutes, 3 coding questions on Codility
tips: Focus on clean, readable code; Codility runs automated test suites for both correctness and performance.
Ensure that memory overhead is strictly controlled.
Check for array index out-of-bounds thoroughly.

rounds.name: Technical Round 1 & 2: DSA & OOD
rounds.format: 45-60 minutes live problem solving and object-oriented design
tips: Apply standard design patterns where appropriate (Factory, Singleton, Observer).
Write modular code with well-encapsulated classes and interfaces.
Demonstrate a solid grasp of Core CS concepts (Threads, Virtual Memory, Inverted Index).
common_topics: Object-Oriented Design (Parking Lot, Elevator, Chess Game)

rounds.name: As-Appropriate (AA) / Hiring Manager Round
rounds.format: 45 minutes high-level technical deep dive, project inquiry, and growth mindset fit
tips: Demonstrate Microsoft's core value: Growth Mindset ('learn-it-all' beats 'know-it-all').
Be prepared to draw architecture diagrams for your college or side projects.
Know Azure fundamentals and general cloud paradigms at a high conceptual level.

general_tips: Microsoft strongly prioritizes code readability, modularity, and maintainability over clever one-liners.
Revise Operating Systems (Silberschatz) and DBMS fundamentals thoroughly before the drive.
Emphasize your willingness to learn new technologies and stacks.

rounds.name: Online Assessment (OA 1 & 2)
rounds.format: Debugging test, 2 DSA questions (70 mins), and Work Style Assessment (Amazon LP)
tips: During the Work Style assessment, strictly choose options that reflect Amazon's Leadership Principles.
In the coding section, aim for 100% test cases passed for both questions.
Don't pick middle-ground answers on the behavioral survey; choose strongly agree or strongly disagree.

rounds.name: Technical Rounds (DSA & Clean Code)
rounds.format: 60 minutes each: 1 DSA problem + 2 Amazon Leadership Principle (LP) behavioral scenarios
tips: Every single round dedicates at least 20 minutes to Amazon Leadership Principles — prepare 2 distinct stories per LP.
Write production-quality code with descriptive variable names and helper functions.
Inquire about scale, traffic, and distributed caching if the question hints at systems.

rounds.name: Bar Raiser Round
rounds.format: 60 minutes with an independent senior interviewer from an outside team
tips: The Bar Raiser evaluates whether you raise the average performance bar of the team.
Deeply reflect 'Customer Obsession', 'Ownership', and 'Dive Deep' in your answers.
Never blame external teammates or past circumstances when describing failed attempts.
common_topics: Bias for Action vs Calculated Risk

general_tips: Memorize all 16 Amazon Leadership Principles and prepare at least 8 versatile STAR-format stories.
Time management is crucial: ensure you have enough time to write full executable code after discussing approaches.
Always optimize for customer experience and operational simplicity.

rounds.name: Aptitude & Coding Assessment
rounds.format: 120 minutes on HackerRank: Math, Probability, CS Fundamentals MCQs, and 2 Coding problems
tips: Brush up on college discrete math, combinatorics, probability, and matrix algebra.
Solve the math MCQs carefully as negative marking or strict sectional cutoffs often apply.
Ensure efficient algorithmic complexity — quadratic solutions will timeout on hidden test cases.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1 & 2
rounds.format: 45-60 minutes live technical problem solving and systems fundamentals
tips: Goldman places extreme value on algorithmic optimization and mathematical rigor.
Be prepared to answer in-depth questions on Java/C++ memory management and garbage collection.
Demonstrate awareness of data structures suited for high-throughput, low-latency applications.
common_topics: Custom Data Structures (e.g., LRU Cache, Median in a Stream)

rounds.name: Values & Behavioral Round
rounds.format: 30-45 minutes with a Vice President evaluating integrity and team culture
tips: Show high ethical standards and accuracy; finance leaves no room for carelessness.
Demonstrate keen curiosity in financial markets and quantitative technology.
Speak about experiences where you collaborated effectively within diverse teams.
common_topics: Why Goldman Sachs & Why Finance Tech?

general_tips: Focus on writing bug-free code on the first attempt with meticulous edge-case handling.
Practice math and logic puzzles on GeeksforGeeks and Brainstellar.
Review Object-Oriented concepts, collections framework, and JVM internals if using Java.

rounds.name: TCS NQT (National Qualifier Test)
rounds.format: Integrated test comprising Foundation Section (Numerical, Reasoning, Verbal) + Advanced Section (Advanced Quant & Coding)
tips: Scoring high in the Advanced section directly qualifies you for the higher-tier Digital or Prime interviews.
Do not spend too long on any single quantitative question; utilize smart elimination.
Ensure that basic coding syntax in your chosen language has zero compilation errors.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.format: 20-30 minutes covering academic syllabus and basic programming
tips: Review your engineering branch basics (even for non-CSE students, explain basic C and SQL).
Be prepared to write code for basic programs like Fibonacci series, prime check, and Armstrong numbers.
Explain your final year/major academic project clearly and your specific individual contributions.
common_topics: SQL Basic Queries (SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY)

rounds.name: Managerial & HR Round
rounds.format: 15-20 minutes behavioral and suitability assessment
tips: Explicitly confirm your willingness to relocate to any TCS office in India.
Affirm your comfort working in rotational shifts and learning any modern technology stack.
Showcase positive attitude, loyalty, and commitment to long-term career growth.

general_tips: A strong performance in the Advanced section of NQT opens up the Digital (7.2 LPA) and Prime (9 LPA) offers.
Practice past TCS NQT question sets on PrepInsta and Youth4work.
Ensure clear, polite, and respectful communication throughout the interview.

rounds.name: Infosys Online Assessment
rounds.format: Sectional test: Mathematical Ability, Logical & Analytical Reasoning, Verbal, and Hands-on Coding
tips: Each section has its own individual cutoff score; manage time equally across sections.
Critical reasoning and data interpretation questions carry high weight.
For coding, pass all default test cases before submitting.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.format: 25-35 minutes covering resume, CS fundamentals, and basic programming
tips: Clearly explain database transactions, normalization (1NF to 3NF), and primary/foreign keys.
Walk through your mini projects with clean diagrams if requested.
Demonstrate clear understanding of your preferred programming language.
common_topics: Web Development Basics (HTML, CSS, JS, REST APIs)

rounds.name: HR Interview
rounds.format: 15-20 minutes verifying candidate credentials, adaptability, and soft skills
tips: Confirm that you are comfortable with pan-India relocation after Mysore campus training.
State your excitement about training at the Infosys Mysore Global Education Center.
Emphasize punctuality, ethics, and team cooperation.
common_topics: Readiness for Mysore Training & Pan-India Relocation

general_tips: Participating in HackWithInfy or InfyTQ certifications provides direct shortcuts to DSE (6.5 LPA) and SP (9.5 LPA) interviews.
Cryptarithmetic and advanced puzzles frequently appear in Infosys aptitude tests — practice these thoroughly.
Be eager and enthusiastic about technology upskilling.

rounds.name: Online Assessment (Deloitte National Test)
rounds.format: 75 minutes: Quantitative Aptitude, Logical Reasoning, Verbal Ability, and Technical MCQs
tips: Deloitte emphasizes verbal ability and analytical business logic.
Review basic cloud, networking, and IT security concepts for the technical MCQ section.
Maintain steady pacing without getting bogged down on complicated arithmetic.

rounds.name: Case Study & Group Discussion Round
rounds.format: 30-40 minutes evaluating team interaction, structured reasoning, and problem formulation
tips: Frame your recommendations logically (Problem Statement -> Analysis -> Recommendation -> Risks).
Encourage less vocal participants politely to show leadership and inclusive teamwork.
Keep interventions concise, factual, and solution-focused.

rounds.name: Partner & HR Round
rounds.format: 30 minutes evaluating consulting fitment, communication polish, and ambition
tips: Present yourself with executive presence, clear diction, and active listening.
Explain how your engineering background complements Deloitte's business advisory services.
Highlight adaptability to varying client cultures and tight deliverables.
common_topics: Leading a Team Under Deadline Pressure

general_tips: Articulate your ideas clearly and concisely — consulting recruiters look for confident client-facing potential.
Understand Deloitte's key service areas: Tech Consulting, Cyber Risk, Enterprise Strategy, and Human Capital.
Maintain high situational awareness and active listening in group rounds.
